label: round3
tail:
Done. Round 3 is complete.

**Terra's objection is correct, for the third time.** `def-real-exponential-function-and-e` defines `exp(x)` and defines `e` only as `exp(1)`; the Statement displays `e^x`, which under `def-real-power` is a different construction, `exp(x log e)`. The item asserted the series expansion of a symbol it never connected to the definition. I verified the bridge against the exact published statements before using it and it closes as you described: `cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals` gives `e = exp(1) > 0`, `def-natural-logarithm` gives `log e = log(exp 1) = 1`, so `def-real-power` yields `e^x = exp(x·1) = exp(x)`. Adjudicated `confirmed_nonfatal`, `dependency_citation`.

**I did not patch step 1.1.** The exhaustive notation audit found the `e^x` bridge **and six more unlicensed uses**:

- radius of convergence and "value at the centre" — uncited (`def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence`)
- `f^(k)` and `C^∞` — uncited, and step 1.2 invoked the Maclaurin definition without ever establishing the smoothness it requires
- `binom(m,0) = 1` — read off nothing (`def-binomial-coefficient`)
- termwise splitting of a convergent series, tagged "algebra" — it's `lem-series-linearity`
- step 1.5 wrote a limit where `thm-ratio-test` asks for a limit superior
- **`[L7]` misquoted the published binomial theorem** — it read `Σ binom(m,n) a^(m-n) b^n` where `thm-binomial-theorem` states `Σ binom(n,k) x^k y^(n-k)`. The coefficient index had been moved to the other variable.

Plus a structural instance of the same defect no gate can see: four steps used the sequence constructed in step 1.3 without citing it, because they sat in the same phase and so *couldn't*. The proof is now strictly stratified across nine phases, so every reuse is an explicit citation; `precheck` confirms that numbering is the canonical one.

Nine facts added ([L17]–[L23] plus rewrites of [L3] and [L7]), nine deps, all published and all earlier in plan order than page 187. No approved statement changed — the six families, the `|x|<1` binomial restriction, the recurrence, and the absence of any `x = ±1` claim all stand. All five plan controls intact.

`precheck` PASS, `rendercheck` OK, `depcheck`/`fwdcheck`/`extcheck` clean repo-wide.

**On the split: defensible, but I don't recommend it, and here's why.** None of the three objections would have been prevented by one. Rounds 1 and 2 live in the binomial half; round 3 lives in the collation half. Each defect would have travelled with its own half into whichever item it landed in. What produced all three was one habit — matching a symbol to its near-neighbour instead of its definition — and that's what the audit addresses, not a seam. I recorded the size facts and the clean seam location in §5 of the report in case you weigh it differently; it's your call and I didn't touch it.

One judgment call worth flagging: the adjudication row records `item_sha256` as `2481ae24…`, the text Terra actually read — matching the round-1/round-2 rows in the same ledger and what `level-coverage.mjs` matches against — with the post-repair hash `b6b4da28…` carried alongside as `repaired_item_sha256`. I read "the round-3 post-repair hash" as the post-round-2-repair text that round 3 judged, which is the same convention; both hashes are in the row either way.

`rejudge-targets.json` now holds this id alone. Ten adjudication rows, ten `confirmed_nonfatal`, zero fatal across all three rounds. The stopping rule is recorded and accepted: a fourth distinct objection closes on the ledger, not with another repair.
